correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all exact Gaussian normal equations for every integer factor and ambient dimension, including boundary R=1 and p=R. Case 1 factorizes into independent Gaussian/chi ratios and gamma moments. Case 2 is a product-normal design/residual quotient; the integrable K0 logarithmic singularity and justified polar dominated-convergence limit give the exact positive \(t^{-R}(\log t)^R\) leading constant, hence the sharp moment cutoff. Dense Gaussian comparison follows by chi small-ball integration. A conditional-variance identity plus strict Jensen proves the MSE gap. The embedded verifier gave 1,513 finite identity and moment-constant diagnostics; finite tests do not prove asymptotics or infinity.

value.rationale: Both structured Gaussian constructions are original source sampling designs and use the identical sketch-row budget R. On a unit-condition-number one-column tensor regression with arbitrary ambient size, \(r_1=r_2=2\) makes factor-reusing mean-square error infinite while independent rows make it finite; the latter retains an exact \((\log t)^R\) tail loss compared with fully independent Gaussian sketches. This is an operationally motivated rare-error/integrability boundary not established by fixed-failure-probability embedding guarantees. No performance or cost dominance is inferred beyond the analyzed error measure.
